outcome: Maternal complications (impending eclampsia, postpartum haemorrhage, discharge without complications)
Neonatal complications (low birth weight, death, requiring observation)
cohort: 92 pregnant women with severe preeclampsia and eclampsia greater than 20 weeks of gestation, admitted to Madras Medical College from August 2017 to July 2018.
finding: Severe preeclampsia was associated with significant maternal complications (e.g., impending eclampsia, postpartum haemorrhage) and neonatal complications (e.g., low birth weight, death).
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the most frequent mode of delivery, accounting for 60.8% of cases.
birth_weight: Most babies weighed between 2-2.5 kg or >= 2.5 kg, with 25% having low birth weight.
gest_age: Participants were >20 weeks of gestation, with most diagnoses occurring between 28 and 34 weeks, and deliveries between 35 and 37 weeks.
